svg.text: #23 — a virtio_net page_pool RX page is released twice
VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(page_ref_count(page) == 0) at skb_release_data+0x1a5, on the node that RECEIVES. No dm-pcache frame in either stack.
1 · allocated — virtio_net refills its RX ring from a page_pool
try_fill_recv [virtio_net] → __page_pool_alloc_netmems_slow
→ alloc_pages_bulk_noprof → get_page_from_freelist
One buffer carries exactly one page reference.
2 · installed as an skb frag — inheriting that one reference
receive_mergeable(): skb_add_rx_frag(skb, i, page, off, len, truesize)
But the same page reaches a SECOND frag, with no second reference.
Usually the two frags sit in different skbs — which is why the frag table
of the crashing skb looks perfectly normal in two of the three captures.
3 · first release — the page goes back to the allocator
skb_defer_free_flush → napi_consume_skb → skb_release_data
→ napi_pp_put_page → __free_frozen_pages
Entirely ordinary. The reference the buffer held is now spent, and the
page is free — while a frag somewhere still points at it.
+9 ms
4 · second release — same path, already-free page
skb_defer_free_flush → napi_consume_skb → skb_release_data
→ __skb_frag_unref → put_page_testzero
→ VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(page_ref_count(page) == 0) ← node dies
A double put of a page_pool RX buffer. Both puts come through the skb layer.
How we know — page_owner=on, printed by dump_page() at the BUG
page last allocated, ts 39011.18 s:
__page_pool_alloc_netmems_slow
try_fill_recv [virtio_net]
virtnet_poll [virtio_net] / net_rx_action
page last free, ts 39169.398 s (BUG at 39169.407 s):
__free_frozen_pages
napi_pp_put_page
skb_release_data
napi_consume_skb / skb_defer_free_flush
The first put leaves no trace in the second skb — only page_owner shows it.
Three captures, one mechanism
capture 1 frags 4 and 6 = same page nr_frags 17
capture 2 no duplicate nr_frags 17
capture 3 no duplicate nr_frags 17
09-11 was the case where both frags happened to land in one skb. The
common fact is the double put, not the duplication.
Why this is not dm-pcache
· Neither the alloc nor the free stack contains a dm-pcache frame.
· Its receive path copies with sock_recvmsg() into a kvec — no page refs.
· Identical crash rate on the copy, MSG_SPLICE_PAGES and MSG_ZEROCOPY
builds; 5 standalone imitations, ~32 rounds, ~2.2 TiB never reproduced it.
Still open
Why the same page reaches two frags. try_fill_recv() handing a page to the
virtqueue twice, or a buffer returned to the ring without re-taking its
reference, both fit. Separating them needs probes inside the refill path.
Caught on the 5th full regression of a loop (5 h 10 min, ~29% of runs hit it). kdump; netconsole and serial capture both suppressed it.
Evidence: repro/evidence/20260916-page-owner/ (plus the 09-11 and 09-15 captures) · archive entry #23
